A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLM4Cov framework and experimental lineage. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CVDP-ECov evaluations, training ablations, execution-filtering experiments, cross-model results, and output-diversity measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds AutoEval-ECov evaluations, CorrectBench comparisons, and refinement-round sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Both versions retain full testbench regeneration from the current state, worst-state selection, coverage-guided rejection, and teacher/imitation/self-sampling training stages. Renaming memoryless transitions as single-step transitions and disclosing the synthesis length do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: v3 adds AutoEval-ECov, comprising 156 VerilogEval-derived tasks using golden RTL and problem specifications for testbench coverage evaluation. The original 83-repository CVDP-ECov benchmark and CodeV-R1 training source remain, substantially broadening evaluated data coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds CorrectBench using Qwen3-235b-A22b-2507 on both benchmarks and Claude 3.5 Sonnet outputs on AutoEval-ECov. These introduce a directly relevant testbench-generation framework beyond the retained model comparisons. Appendix D also adds an as-reported TBnTB comparison, explicitly using different evaluation conditions.

E3.justification: The original three-round agentic and single-pass direct evaluation settings remain. Added evaluations introduce AutoEval-ECov's 100% coverage threshold, re-evaluation of supplied CorrectBench outputs, and a zero-to-three-round sensitivity sweep. Newly listed decoding parameters document settings without establishing changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused refinement-round sensitivity analysis for the teacher, base model, and three training stages in Table 3. Existing state-history, trajectory-generation, state-selection, progressive-training, execution-filtering, cross-model, and output-diversity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify Pass@1 with five generated samples and list training seed 42. Neither adds repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; the additional results use the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: All 14 retained model/stage rows preserve their four CVDP-ECov scores. v3 adds extensive AutoEval-ECov results, CorrectBench comparisons, and round-wise outcomes. Table 2 reports Stage 2 AutoEval-ECov pass rate/average coverage of 85.0%/96.3%, whereas Appendix D's Table 7 reports 84.0%/96.5% while claiming agreement; these new values are internally inconsistent.

T1.justification: The state definition, conditional-independence assumption, rejection rule, and staged supervised objective remain equivalent. Some explicit trajectory and pooled-data equations are replaced by prose or diagrams preserving their meaning. The added discussion of standard Markov modeling introduces no new formal assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions and 69.2% coverage-pass claim remain. The abstract narrows its characterization of online RL from impractical to less practical in certain scenarios and highlights the 90.4% average coverage already reported in v1. These are limited changes in qualification and emphasis.

C2.justification: v3 interprets refinement gains as saturating after two to three rounds and relates its minimal state representation to context compression. New Appendix D discusses protocol, simulator, and model-access limitations of prior-method comparisons, while still claiming an advantage from unmatched TBnTB results. The original RL-compatibility discussion is retained as Appendix E.

D1.justification: New Table 4 lists model-specific temperature and top-p settings. Section 3.3 newly specifies two-step dataset synthesis, and Section 4.2 explains the inherited VerilogEval decontamination. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware, data counts, simulator versions, and implementation-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against offline agent learning through AgentBank, AgentPro, QLASS, and EDGE, distinguishing directly scored transitions from long-horizon credit assignment. It adds connections to long-context and history-compression research, references VerilogEval, and develops explicit comparisons with CorrectBench and TBnTB beyond their earlier related-work mentions.

P1.justification: Targeted edits replace memoryless with single-step, Cov Pass with Pass Rate, and Sim Pass with Syn Pass. The trajectory taxonomy and training-progression discussion move from Section 3.3 to 3.4. Disclosure text and a baseline-comparison appendix are added, but most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with explicit model and training flows, and new Figures 4–5 illustrate trajectory types and staged synthesis. Table 2 replaces improvement columns with a second benchmark and adds CorrectBench rows. New round-sensitivity, decoding-configuration, and baseline-comparison tables substantially expand the displays; existing plots are also relabeled and relocated.

improvement.justification: The second benchmark, relevant CorrectBench comparisons, round-sensitivity analysis, and decoding details provide broader empirical support and clearer documentation than v1. These gains are qualified by conflicting AutoEval-ECov values in Tables 2 and 7, inconsistent teacher identification in Table 3, and superiority claims based on unmatched TBnTB conditions. The revision offers a limited net benefit, with unresolved reliability issues in some added evidence.
